vision_features.image_context: Close-up view of a broad-leafed plant, showing multiple leaves. The image focuses on two to three large, ovate leaves in the foreground, with additional leaves and stems visible in the background. The plant appears to be a legume, likely soybean or bean, based on leaf shape and hairy stem texture. Both upper leaf surfaces are clearly visible.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. White-to-pale-grey powdery or dusty coating: Present across large portions of the upper surface of the foreground leaves, particularly the left and center leaves. Coverage is diffuse and somewhat patchy, spreading across broad areas of the leaf surface including the interveinal spaces. The coating appears flat to very slightly raised, with a matte, dusty texture. Patches range from small (approx. 10–20 mm) to large confluent areas covering much of the leaf blade. No distinct border or halo around individual patches — they blend gradually into green tissue. The coating gives affected areas a whitish-grey, frosted appearance over the underlying green.

2. Small reddish-brown to dark brown pinpoint dots: Scattered densely across the upper surface of the center and left foreground leaves, distributed over both the affected whitish-grey areas and some greener areas. Individual dots are approximately 0.5–1.5 mm in diameter, roughly circular, and appear slightly raised or embedded within the pale coating. They are dark reddish-brown to near-black in color with no visible lighter border. They are distributed in a scattered, relatively uniform pattern across the leaf surface, with concentration appearing heaviest in areas with the pale coating.

3. Pale, washed-out green coloration in coated areas: Where the whitish-grey coating is present, the underlying leaf tissue appears paler, lighter green compared to unaffected areas and background leaves. This is most pronounced on the left foreground leaf.

4. Minor leaf tearing/physical damage: A small irregular tear or crack is visible near the upper right area of the center foreground leaf, approximately 10–15 mm long. No associated discoloration around the tear.
vision_features.absences:
1. No visible yellowing (pale yellow discoloration) of leaf tissue surrounding the abnormal markings or in the general leaf blade.
2. No raised blister-like pustules or orange/rust-colored powdery deposits visible on the leaf surface.
3. No visible dark, angular, water-soaked or brown dead patches with defined sharp margins typical of tissue that has completely dried out.
4. No visible abnormalities on leaf undersides (undersides are not shown), and no drooping or wilting of stems or petioles visible in the image.
vision_features.summary: The most prominently affected leaves display a widespread pale whitish-grey, dusty, matte coating covering large portions of the upper leaf surface, giving a frosted appearance. Scattered densely across this coating — and on adjacent green areas — are numerous tiny reddish-brown to near-black pinpoint dots approximately 0.5–1.5 mm in diameter. The two central foreground leaves are most severely affected, with the coating covering well over half their total surface area. The single most striking visual feature is the dense distribution of tiny dark reddish-brown dots embedded within and around the pale dusty coating across the leaf surface.
